title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from p.24). k is a ring and S = k{T} is the divided-power polynomial algebra in one variable, graded in degrees >= 0, with T^(i) T^(j) = c_ij T^(i+j), where c_ij = binom(i+j, i). For a k-module M, the 'shadow' of order N is ω_N(M) = τ_{>=N}(M ⊗_k S) = S^{+(N)} · (M ⊗_k S). Here S^{+(N)} = ⊕_{i>=N} S_i.

On p.24 Grothendieck proved that ω_N : k-Mod → (graded S-Mod) is fully faithful. A morphism ω_N(M) → ω_N(M') is a family (u_i)_{i>=N} subject to c_ij (u_{i+j} − u_i) = 0 for i >= N, j >= 1. An arithmetic lemma on binomial coefficients then forces all u_i to be equal. He also noted a right adjoint π_N, given by compatible families (x_i)_{i>=N}.

This page draws the conclusions.
(i) The ω_N get 'coarser' as N grows, since they forget more low-degree information, yet each is still fully faithful.
(ii) Truncations τ_N are not fully faithful in general. They are the identity on graded modules concentrated in degrees >= N, which he calls 'virtual shadows of order N−1'.
(iii) He introduces Omb(k), the category of 'virtual shadows': graded S-modules, perhaps in degrees >= 0. He also introduces Omb_{N-tr}(k), the full subcategory of 'N-negligible' modules (M_i = 0 for i >= N).
(iv) Omb_{N-tr} is thick (a Serre subcategory). The Gabriel quotient Omb/Omb_{N-tr} is canonically equivalent to the category N-Omb of graded S-modules with M_i = 0 for i < N.
- Check: in the quotient, Hom(M, M') = colim Hom(M_1, M'/M'') with M/M_1 and M'' negligible. Since S is nonnegatively graded, τ_{>=N}M is a submodule, so the colimit is Hom(τ_N M, τ_N M').
- Hence the quotient functor is identified with truncation τ_N.
- τ_N(M) is a subobject of M functorially, and the quotient functor has a right adjoint (the section functor). This is the φ_N / φ_{0N} of the next page. It is computed there degreewise as Hom^i(τ_{N−i}S, −), together with the Ext-vanishing that makes M ⊗ S 'φ-closed'.
(v) A shadow is called 'negligible' if it is a filtered union of N-negligible ones for variable N. Equivalently, every homogeneous x is killed by S^{+(N)} for some N, i.e. it is torsion for the degree filtration {S^{+(N)}}. This is again a thick subcategory, and he starts to describe the localized category.

Purpose: this is the exact analogue of Serre's FAC description of quasi-coherent sheaves on Proj as graded modules modulo 'eventually zero' modules (QGr), carried out for the divided-power algebra. The theorem to be proved (next page) says that M ⊗ S is closed (local) for each localization. Together with full faithfulness of ω_N, this embeds k-Mod into the 'Proj-like' localized category of graded Γ(T)-modules. That serves his study of the divided-power de Rham complex (1976 IHÉS lecture).
errors: The displayed adjunction 'Hom_Omb(N, τ_N(M)) ≃ Hom_{N-Omb}(τ_N(N), τ_N(M))' (reading the second argument as τ_N of the source) is false as stated. A morphism of truncated modules τ_N𝒩 → τ_N M need not extend by zero to 𝒩 → τ_N M, because S-linearity links degrees < N to degrees >= N. Correct statements are: (a) τ_N : Omb → N-Omb is right adjoint to the inclusion, Hom_Omb(P, M) = Hom(P, τ_N M) for P in N-Omb; (b) the quotient functor has a right adjoint (section functor) φ_N. This φ_N is NOT the inclusion of τ_N M, and it is what the next page computes. The text itself flags uncertainty ('Hom_{N-Omb} ou Omb').
Notational clash: N denotes both the integer and the graded module in the Hom formula.
Hesitation over whether Omb should require degrees >= 0 ('[à degrés >= 0 ?]'), while the negligibility condition is written with 'for all i in Z'. This is harmless but unresolved on the page.
'τ_N ... pas = sur la sous-catégorie' is garbled. The intended statement is that τ_N is the identity, hence fully faithful, on modules vanishing in degrees < N.

ideas.what: Shadow functors ω_N(M) = τ_{>=N}(M ⊗ Γ_k(T)) are fully faithful from k-modules to graded Γ(T)-modules, with a right adjoint π_N given by compatible families
ideas.modern_name: fully faithful embedding of k-Mod into graded modules over the divided-power line (quasi-coherent sheaves on G_a^♯/G_m-type objects)
ideas.usually_credited_to: no standard attribution; this specific statement seems not to be in the literature

ideas.what: Serre/Gabriel quotient of graded S-modules by the thick subcategory of N-negligible modules, identified with truncation τ_N, with a right-adjoint section functor
ideas.modern_name: Gabriel localization; truncation as quotient functor
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gabriel (1962), Serre FAC (1955) for graded modules

ideas.what: 'Negligible' shadows = torsion for the degree filtration S^{+(N)} (not the S^+-adic filtration, which differs over Z since T^N = N! T^(N)); localization by them
ideas.modern_name: QGr / noncommutative Proj (Artin–Zhang style) for the divided power algebra Γ(T) with the PD-degree filtration
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (FAC), Artin–Zhang (1994) for the general formalism

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a 'Proj' / QGr formalism for graded modules over the divided-power polynomial algebra Γ_k(T), localizing at torsion for the PD-degree filtration. The aim is to embed k-Mod fully faithfully and to compute the local objects via Ext-vanishing against τ_{N−i}S. Graded Γ(T)-modules are essentially G_m-equivariant modules over the divided-power additive group G_a^♯. Stacks of this kind (G_a^♯, G_a^♯/G_m) are central to recent Drinfeld and Bhatt–Lurie work on prismatization and de Rham/Hodge–Tate stacks, and Grothendieck uses this in a divided-power de Rham context. As far as I know the 1976 'ombres' formalism has never been connected to that literature.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is an early, unpublished instance of studying quasi-coherent objects over the graded divided-power line, i.e. G_a^♯-type geometry, for de Rham purposes. The question of what the 'negligible'-localized category is (a Proj of Γ_Z(T), which is subtle over Z) is left open on this page.

missed.claim: Identifying the localized category Omb/(negligible) is left unfinished at the bottom of the page. Over Q it is just k-Mod, but over Z or F_p the Proj of Γ(T) with respect to the PD filtration is nontrivial.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A clean description would clarify the relation between divided-power graded modules and filtered or crystalline linear algebra in mixed characteristic.

deep.surprise_reason: Most of the page is a standard Serre/Gabriel localization of graded modules. What is mildly notable is applying it to the divided-power algebra with the 'ombres' language as a tool for the PD de Rham complex, which prefigures G_a^♯-type considerations. The ideas are still generic enough that a specialist would not be strongly surprised.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely begins 'En ce sens les foncteurs "ombres" ω_N sont d'autant plus grossiers ...'.
'ils sont donc pleinement fidèles' is more plausibly 'ils sont tous pleinement fidèles, alors que les foncteurs τ_N ne sont pas pl. fidèles bien sûr, sauf sur la sous-catégorie ...'.
'Le foncteur [?] au quotient' should read 'Le foncteur passage au quotient'.
'admet un adjoint : droite (cf. fid. comme de [?])' is likely 'admet un adjoint à droite (cf. pl. fid. comme on peut ... )'; uncertain.
The marginal insertion near 'négligeable' reads approximately 'plus [?]' or 'si elle est lim→ d'ombres N-négligeables'.
